defects.summary: The MOD-027 gold-sync tests are still written for the old five-column fact grain. The approved MOD-028 design (AMD-007, RULE-155/RULE-164) adds payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id to silv_daily_count_detail and to the fact's grain and unique clustered index, so these tests need amending where they name the grain.
defects.steps_to_reproduce: run_suite; test_MOD027 TC-027-001 to -010 and -012 fail. Reproduce: EXEC test_MOD027.SetUp; insert TC-027-001's five detail rows with payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id = 0; EXEC Layercake.usp_load_fact_daily_member_count_detail; the fact rows equal TC-027-001's #Expected (with 0,0,0 in the new columns). Without the ids the load raises 515.
defects.expected: Under the 'Daily count payment segments' answer, the MOD-027 tests keep passing, "changed only where they name the grain". Silver detail rows and fact rows carry the three ids (NOT NULL). The fact has 16 columns and a unique clustered index on the eight grain columns (DES-001).
defects.actual: TC-027-001 to TC-027-010 (except -011) put rows into the faked silv_daily_count_detail without the three ids. FakeTable drops NOT NULL, so the ids are NULL, and usp_load_fact_daily_member_count_detail fails with 515 ('Cannot insert the value NULL into column payment_method_id, table #det_stage'). The real table cannot hold such rows. TC-027-012 expects 13 fact columns and a 5-column clustered index; the built fact has 16 columns and the 8-column index the design specifies (TC-028-001 and TC-028-003 pass). Checked with run_sql: TC-027-001's data with 0 in the three ids gives exactly the test's expected 4 fact rows and the log 'Success' 4/0/0. So the sync behaves correctly once the setup carries the new grain.

defects.summary: MOD-022's first-run drift test seeds pre-existing silv_daily_count_detail rows at the old grain (no segment ids), so under the approved MOD-028 grain the load reads every seeded cell as a different cell from the ones it derives.
defects.steps_to_reproduce: run_suite; test_MOD022 TC-022-019 fails. EXEC test_MOD022.SetUp; run TC-022-019's inserts, adding payment_method_id/payer_type_id/concession_type_id = 0 to the detail rows; EXEC Layercake.usp_load_silv_daily_count; SELECT from silv_daily_count_adjustment: the 4 expected rows.
defects.expected: Under the approved design, detail cells carry the three ids (not null), so a pre-existing cell for a contact with no attributes is (…, 0, 0, 0). With that, the run writes exactly the test's 4 expected drift adjustments.
defects.actual: The seeded rows have NULL ids (faked table). The run writes 12 adjustment rows: -1 active for each NULL-id cell and the full figures for each derived (0,0,0) cell, instead of the 4 drift rows. Checked with run_sql: the same data with 0 in the three ids on the seeded rows gives exactly the 4 expected rows (2022-11-01 c1 pe+1 rn+1; 2023-06-15 c1 pe+1; 2023-06-15 c2 p+1; 2025-01-10 c1 pe+1 rn+1). The test's #Expected and #Mismatch also leave out the three ids.

defects.summary: The MOD-021 structure tests for silv_daily_count_adjustment still expect the old columns and a unique key on run_id plus the six-column cell. The approved MOD-028 design adds the three segment ids to the table and to its unique key.
defects.steps_to_reproduce: run_suite; test_MOD021 TC-021-015 and TC-021-017 fail. Look at sys.indexes / sys.columns for Layercake.silv_daily_count_adjustment.
defects.expected: DES-001 silv_daily_count_adjustment (AMD-007, RULE-155/RULE-162): the three segment columns are int not null, and the table is unique on (run_id, [date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id).
defects.actual: The built table matches the design: UQ_Layercake_silv_daily_count_adjustment_run_id_cell on run_id, date, region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id; the three new columns are present (TC-028-002 passes). TC-021-015 fails on the column list. TC-021-017 finds 0 unique indexes keyed exactly on the old 7 columns.

defects.summary: MOD-016's Phase 1 column-list test still expects silv_daily_count_detail (15 columns) and fact_daily_member_count_detail (13 columns) at the Phase 1 grain. The approved MOD-028 design (AMD-007) adds payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id to both.
defects.steps_to_reproduce: run_suite; test_MOD016 TC-016-014 fails. SELECT column_id, name FROM sys.columns WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID('Layercake.silv_daily_count_detail').
defects.expected: DES-001 after MOD-028: silv_daily_count_detail has 18 columns, and fact_daily_member_count_detail has 16 columns with the three segment ids. Mike's 'Daily count payment segments' answer explicitly changes this grain. The annual rate base tables stay unchanged.
defects.actual: silv_daily_count_detail has its 15 Phase 1 columns in their old order, then payment_method_id (16), payer_type_id (17) and concession_type_id (18); the fact gains the same three. The fact_annual_rate_base and silv_annual_rate_base rows of the test still match. The test fails only on the detail and fact lists.
